blocker_shred_surrogate_child_keys.failure_mode_note: {spine:KEY_HASH} is a per-row hash minted by the shred layer and is NOT stable across reloads. On the next shred rebuild the same business fact is re-hashed, its child key CHANGES, and the build INSERTS A NEW CHILD ROW instead of closing and versioning the existing one. The satellite accumulates duplicates and stops being a history. Every gate passes because the key IS resolved -- deterministic, on-row, non-renumbering. Resolution and stability are different properties and no gate here measures the second.
blocker_shred_surrogate_child_keys.do_not_fabricate_note: At SATELLITE grain 6 of 7 (satellite, leg) pairs carry both a surrogate and a business form, which LOOKS convertible. At VIEW grain the overlap is EMPTY -- 0 of 45. A leg can only name a column present on its own view. On SAT_POLICY_CERTIFICATE the apparent business form is a MEMBER-identifier ladder, so converting would merge every certificate of one member onto one child row.

spreadsheet_summary.classification_discipline_note: Classes were DERIVED from content and every non-prose class was PROVED by round-tripping a real value. Two earlier passes of this step over-reported prose (22, then 12) and both were false accusations -- the worst being 'Source Column', whose only 4 non-matching values are 2D_ECHO, 2D_ECO, 2D_ECHO_CTMT and 64VB_STATUS: real Oracle column names that START WITH A DIGIT. spreadsheet_summary.prose_detection_note: Prose was identified by CLASS, never by a '_note' suffix test. self_assertion.rule_note: A machine-readable value carries a _token suffix and MUST contain no whitespace -- that is a hard FAILURE naming its key. Every other space-bearing string is REPORTED for review, never failed: the first draft of this assertion would have fired on natural_key_convention's legitimate pattern and on every genuine attribute name like 'Classification Effective Date'. A space is not the property; being READ AS A TOKEN is.
